literature_notes: XKR4 is a 10-TM scramblase with both its N-terminus (residues 1-112) and C-terminus (residues 510-650) on the intracellular face. All five extracellular loops are very short (5-11 aa: ECL1 135-142, ECL2 327-333, ECL3 394-398, ECL4 449-456, ECL5 478-488) and none of the three ledger lines reports a tag insertion in any of them. L1 describes full-length mouse Xkr4 and human XKR4 constructs carrying N-terminal V5 and/or C-terminal FLAG tags — both termini are intracellular, so these are intracellular tags only. L2 describes a C-terminal TEV-FLAG-6xHis purification construct, again intracellular. L3 describes GFP-tagged XKR family members used for FSEC screening; the context ('C-terminal caspase cleavage site distal from the membrane') implies a C-terminal GFP, which is also intracellular. No ledger line reports any tag insertion at an extracellular position for XKR4 or a close ortholog. Zero surface tag sites qualify.

literature_other_positions.note: N-terminal V5 tag on full-length human and mouse XKR4; the N-terminus (residues 1-112) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the cell surface.
C-terminal FLAG tag on mouse Xkr4 (and C-terminal FLAG-6xHis in L2); the C-terminus (residues 510-650) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so these tags face the cytoplasm.
GFP-tagged hXkr4 used for FSEC; context implies C-terminal fusion, which is intracellular; construct confirmed functional for apoptotic scrambling but the tag is not on the extracellular face.
